Ticket T-8007: the board project page flaps between 'Live' and 'connecting' every few seconds (owner report from the MacBook board; the board server is NOT restarting, pid up 4h, /api/health answers in ~1 ms). ROOT CAUSE found by the coordinator: two timers write the same chip (#liveText/#liveDot). tools/watch-assets/project.js sets it every 250 ms from window.__swarmProjectOkAt (marked by /api/project and /api/live responses), while tools/watch-assets/project-live.js chip() overwrites it every 1 s from its OWN lastOkAt, which stays 0 while the Live tab is hidden (load() returns early) so it writes 'connecting'. Fix: (1) exactly one owner of the chip: project.js; project-live.js must not write #liveText/#liveDot at all, only mark window.__swarmProjectOkAt on a good /api/live answer (it already does via the fetch wrapper; keep its own lastOkAt only for its Stale-data logic). (2) Add to tools/watch-assets/board-lib.js a pure chipState({ lastOkAt, now, pollMs, everOk }) returning 'live' | 'stale' | 'connecting': 'connecting' only before the first good answer has ever arrived; after that, 'live' until TWO poll intervals have been missed (age > two times pollMs + slack of the request timeout), then 'stale' with its age. Use it in project.js with pollMs = its poll interval. Do not change liveness() behavior for other callers. (3) Server event stream heartbeat (tools/watch-server.mjs openEvents, used by run pages through tools/watch-assets/app.js EventSource): write an SSE comment line ': ping

' to every open stream about every 10 s (injectable interval / now so tests drive it), cleared on close; the heartbeat must not call getRunSnapshot. Also stop the stream being dropped by node's server timeouts: set server.keepAliveTimeout/headersTimeout sensibly and res.socket.setTimeout(0)/setKeepAlive for event streams. In app.js the client shows 'connecting' only after 2 missed heartbeats (no message or ping for > 2 x 10 s plus slack); track pings via the raw stream (EventSource does not surface comments, so ALSO send a named 'ping' event 'event: ping
data: {}

' instead of or in addition to the comment, and listen for it). (4) Do not slow the polls: /api/project and /api/live reads stay as they are. Tests in tests/board-live-chip.test.mjs: chipState with a slow read (answer arriving after 1 missed poll stays live; after 2 missed polls becomes stale; never 'connecting' after the first good answer), a static check that project-live.js does not write liveText/liveDot, the server writes a ping on an idle stream after the interval and stops after close, and the client logic (a pure helper exported from board-lib.js, e.g. streamState({ lastMessageAt, now, heartbeatMs })) flips to connecting only after 2 missed heartbeats. Keep existing tests in context passing. Do NOT touch tools/swarm.mjs, the tools/swarm folder, package files or .github. Tests: node:test, injected deps or fake timers (no real waiting, no network beyond a loopback test server the existing tests already use); never write token-shaped literals. Run `node --import ./tests/_isolate-config.mjs --test <your tests and the existing tests named in context>` and `node tools/check-package.mjs`. If a rule cannot be met inside your outputs, return blocked. Tests listed in ignoreTests only use these files for unrelated behavior; the coordinator runs the FULL suite after integration.
